title: Control-plane tombstone propagation caused geo misaffinity and unintended variant escalation — postmortem
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Summary: On 2026-02-19 a control-plane tombstone (decommission marker) that should have been transient became durable in the zone-weight aggregator cache, marking a healthy EU region as 'do-not-send'. Traffic routing logic treated the region as unavailable, rehoming traffic to other regions and triggering our compatibility-based variant substitution rules. This led to a sudden increase in requests routed to smaller/quantized model variants in other regions, causing higher latencies, tokenization mismatches on some prompts, and a 3x cost spike for a subset of customers during the 45-minute window.
detection: On-call pager alerted at 2026-02-19T14:12Z for a 120% increase in p99 generation latency and abnormal model-variant mix change. Console dashboards showed an abrupt drop in EU production egress and a correlated rise in inter-region egress. Customer SLO alerts started firing for several enterprise tenants. On-call runbook lookup pointed to recent weight-aggregation deploy at 2026-02-19T13:47Z.
timeline: 2026-02-19T13:47Z: weight-aggregator v2 deployed with a cache rewrite. 2026-02-19T13:55Z: one zone in EU emitted a transient decommission marker during rolling upgrade. 2026-02-19T13:56Z: aggregator incorrectly persisted marker to Redis with infinite TTL due to a missing expiry flag in new code path. 2026-02-19T14:04Z: routing service read the tombstone and reduced EU region weight to zero. 2026-02-19T14:12Z: on-call alert for p99 latency. 2026-02-19T14:13Z: incident declared; mitigation: operator manually cleared tombstone from Redis and rolled forward a hotfix to the aggregator. 2026-02-19T14:58Z: traffic normalization confirmed; final verification and post-incident review scheduled.
impact: Duration: ~44 minutes of degraded routing. Effected metrics: p99 latency for text generation increased from 220ms to 1.9s for impacted tenants; token costs for routed workload rose by ~310% due to cross-region egress and variant substitutions; 17 enterprise customers experienced SLO violations, two opened support escalations. No data exfiltration; no request bodies lost, but a small subset (~0.6% of requests) received inconsistent tokenization due to variant mismatch.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Removed the tombstone key from Redis to restore region weight. 2) Applied a temporary routing override to pin high-priority tenants to original region while restoring capacity. 3) Rolled back weight-aggregator cache rewrite to previous stable version in canary and then prod. 4) Notified Customer Support and posted status updates to affected customers.
root_cause: A change in the weight-aggregator introduced a path that wrote decommission markers to Redis without setting TTL. The code assumed upstream callers would set expiry; a refactor removed that responsibility transfer. Result: a transient decommission became persistent until manual intervention. The routing layer treats persisted tombstones as durable unavailability, inducing automatic regional failover and downstream model-variant substitution logic to select 'compatible' but smaller variants in target regions.
contributing_factors: 1) Missing unit test covering Redis key TTL behavior. 2) Lack of a defensive TTL enforcement in aggregator write path. 3) Routing layer lacks a heuristics-driven cooldown for sudden regional weight zeroing (it immediately rehomes traffic). 4) Variant substitution policies are aggressive under sudden capacity loss and do not consult recent latency or tokenization compatibility metrics.
long_term_fix: Planned fixes (see PRs): 1) Enforce TTL at write time in weight-aggregator and add integration tests for Redis key lifecycle. 2) Add a defensive guard in routing controller: ignore single-interval weight zeros unless corroborated by health pings over 2 minutes. 3) Introduce a 'soft-failover' path that drains a fraction of traffic before full region cutover to observe variant substitution effects. 4) Update variant substitution policy to consult tokenization compatibility matrix and recent latency deltas before promoting compact variants. 5) Add a dashboard alarm for unexpected durable tombstones.
corrective_actions_taken: 1) Hotfix deployed to weight-aggregator to restore TTL behavior (PR #11267). 2) Emergency playbook updated to include TTL linting for cache writes. 3) Routing override automation added to incident toolkit to quickly pin traffic per-customer. 4) Postmortem reviewed with SRE, Routing, Runtime, and Product; action owners assigned.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-82145: Add TTL enforcement and tests to weight-aggregator (owner: Marco Liu, due: 2026-03-21)
ENG-82146: Implement routing cooldown heuristic and canary evaluation (owner: Elena Kostov, due: 2026-03-28)
ENG-82147: Revise variant substitution policy to include tokenization compatibility checks (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-04-04)
ENG-82148: Dashboard and alert for durable tombstone anomalies (owner: Observability Team, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-82149: Runbook drill and pager rotation update to include this failure mode (owner: SRE Lead, due: 2026-03-15)
lessons_learned: 1) Persisting transient control-plane signals can have outsized operational impact; guard rails are necessary. 2) Cross-team testing (routing + aggregator + runtime variant policies) would have caught the interaction. 3) Automated rollback is useful, but for stateful control-plane writes we also need verification and TTL checks. 4) Customers with strict SLOs should be offered a regional pinning option as a commercial feature to avoid automatic rehoming during control-plane turbulence.
notes: This ticket captures the engineering postmortem. A separate customer-facing incident summary was published by Support and Communications. Eng leads agreed to treat 'durable tombstone' as a documented failure mode in the routing SLA playbook.
assessments: Risk: medium for reoccurrence until TTL enforcement and routing cooldowns are in place. Cost: estimated engineering ~1.5 engineer-months across teams to implement long-term fixes. Business: short-term reputational impact with a handful of enterprise customers; mitigated by CS outreach and credits.
verification_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests added to CI for TTL semantics. 2) Canary rollout of aggregator v2 with synthetic tombstone injection tests to validate routing cooldown response. 3) Post-deploy increase in monitoring retention for tombstone keys and an automated histogram of region-weight delta frequency.
postmortem_reviewed_by: Elena Kostov, Priya Nair, SRE Lead (Jordan Park), Product Lead (Marco Vega)
